statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-53666 (GHSA-337j-9hxr-rhxg): react-router's deserializeErrors(), which rebuilds errors from server-rendered hydration data, calls the constructor named by an error's __subType, so in applications doing server-side rendering and hydration an attacker who can shape those errors could trigger unexpected constructor execution in the browser. The advisory says it does not affect applications using Declarative Mode and only affects Framework Mode and Data Mode applications doing manual SSR or hydration. It is fixed in react-router 7.18.0 by commit 9d22943, which limits __subType to a list of supported error types: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/security/advisories/GHSA-337j-9hxr-rhxg, https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/commit/9d22943fd46c8ae4b08236425fa3549e10e9ad1a, https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/releases/tag/react-router@7.18.0 . We read every published jaeger-dev package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository: 21 builds, 2.19.0-r1 to the current 2.23.0-r4, each for x86_64 and aarch64, every download checked against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/jaeger, a Go program. That program embeds the prebuilt assets of the jaeger-ui release with the same version number as gzip-compressed files; we decompressed every gzip stream in /usr/bin/jaeger and searched the JavaScript. Every build of one Jaeger version carries an identical bundle, and a search of the uncompressed binary finds none of the strings below, so there is no uncompressed copy. The bundle sets __reactRouterVersion to 7.16.0 in 2.19.0-r1 to 2.19.0-r4, 7.18.0 in 2.20.0-r0 to 2.20.0-r5 and 7.18.2 from 2.21.0-r0, matching the react-router versions locked by jaeger-ui v2.19.0 and v2.20.0 and later: https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/blob/v2.19.0/package-lock.json, https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/blob/v2.20.0/pnpm-lock.yaml . jaeger-ui mounts its routes with the declarative <BrowserRouter> component, not a data router: https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/blob/v2.19.0/packages/jaeger-ui/src/index.tsx, https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/blob/v2.23.0/packages/jaeger-ui/src/index.tsx . In every build the bundle contains neither the __subType property that deserializeErrors reads nor the window.__staticRouterHydrationData global from which react-router's data routers load hydration data, so the hydration and error-deserialization code was left out of the bundle. As a positive control, the published react-router 7.16.0, 7.18.0 and 7.18.2 npm packages contain both strings, and the same bundle search finds other react-router code in every build (the __reactRouterVersion assignment and the absolute-URL expression). The vulnerable code is therefore not in any published build of this package.
